topic: Turning 26 in Florida 2026: State Extension Rules and SEP Guide

title.en: Turning 26 in Florida: Health Insurance Options 2026
title.es: Cumpliendo 26 en Florida: Opciones de Seguro Medico 2026

description.en: Florida law may extend your parent's plan to age 30. If not, you have 60 days from coverage loss to enroll in ACA Marketplace or other 2026 coverage.
description.es: La ley de Florida puede extender el plan hasta los 30. Si no, tiene 60 dias desde la perdida de cobertura para inscribirse en opciones 2026.

h1.en: Turning 26 in Florida in 2026? Here Are All Your Health Insurance Options
h1.es: Cumpliendo 26 en Florida en 2026? Aqui Estan Todas Sus Opciones de Seguro Medico

subhero.en: Florida F.S. 627.6562 lets qualifying adults stay on a fully-insured parent plan through the year they turn 30. If that extension does not apply, you have 60 days from losing coverage to enroll in a new ACA Marketplace plan through healthcare.gov.
subhero.es: La ley de Florida F.S. 627.6562 permite que adultos calificados permanezcan en el plan totalmente asegurado de un padre hasta el ano en que cumplen 30. Si esa extension no aplica, tiene 60 dias desde la perdida de cobertura para inscribirse en un nuevo plan del Mercado ACA.

heading.en: You have 60 days from your coverage loss date to enroll in new coverage
heading.es: Tiene 60 dias desde la fecha de perdida de cobertura para inscribirse

body.en: Your 60-day Special Enrollment Period (SEP) at healthcare.gov opens the day you lose parent-plan coverage and closes 60 days later. For example, if your Florida parent plan drops you on August 31, 2026, your SEP window runs from August 31 through October 29, 2026. Miss that window and you must wait until the 2027 ACA Open Enrollment Period starting November 1, 2026, unless another qualifying life event occurs.
body.es: Su Periodo de Inscripcion Especial (SEP) de 60 dias en healthcare.gov comienza el dia que pierde la cobertura del plan de sus padres y cierra 60 dias despues. Por ejemplo, si el plan de Florida de sus padres lo da de baja el 31 de agosto de 2026, su ventana SEP va del 31 de agosto al 29 de octubre de 2026.

label.en: Florida age-30 extension (state-regulated plans only, if you qualify)
label.es: Extension de Florida hasta los 30 (solo planes regulados por el estado, si califica)

label.en: Employer plan SEP (if offered at your new job)
label.es: SEP del plan del empleador (si se ofrece en su trabajo)

label.en: Florida Medicaid (pregnant women, children, limited adult categories; year-round)
label.es: Medicaid de Florida (mujeres embarazadas, ninos, categorias adultas limitadas; todo el ano)

quickAnswer.en: Turning 26 in Florida activates a qualifying life event and a 60-day Special Enrollment Period to get your own health coverage. Florida adds one option most states lack: Florida Insurance Law (F.S. 627.6562) allows you to stay on a fully-insured parent plan through the end of the calendar year you turn 30, if you are unmarried, have no dependents, are a Florida resident or student, and carry no other coverage. If that extension does not apply (most large-employer plans are self-insured under ERISA and exempt), your main 2026 options are: an ACA Marketplace plan with premium tax credits at healthcare.gov, employer-sponsored coverage at your own job (30-day window), or COBRA continuation at 102 percent of the full premium. Florida has not expanded Medicaid, so most single childless 26-year-olds do not qualify for Florida Medicaid unless pregnant or disabled. ACA subsidies are available for incomes from 100 percent to 400 percent FPL ($15,960 to $63,840 for a single person in 2026). The 2026 ACA subsidy cliff returned after enhanced premium tax credits expired January 1, 2026.
quickAnswer.es: Cumplir 26 en Florida activa un evento calificador y un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial de 60 dias para obtener su propia cobertura de salud. Florida agrega una opcion que la mayoria de los estados no tienen: la Ley de Seguros de Florida (F.S. 627.6562) le permite permanecer en el plan totalmente asegurado de un padre hasta el fin del ano calendario en que cumple 30, si no esta casado, no tiene dependientes, es residente de Florida o estudiante, y no tiene otra cobertura. Si esa extension no aplica, sus principales opciones 2026 son: un plan del Mercado ACA con creditos fiscales de prima en healthcare.gov, cobertura patrocinada por empleador en su propio trabajo (ventana de 30 dias), o continuacion COBRA al 102 por ciento de la prima completa.

introParagraphs.en: Turning 26 is the federal age at which dependent coverage on a parent's health plan must end under the Affordable Care Act. For most Americans, that birthday creates a 60-day Special Enrollment Period (SEP) and forces a search for individual health insurance. Florida residents face this same SEP clock, but with an important state-law overlay: Florida Insurance Statute F.S. 627.6562 requires insurers of state-regulated, fully-insured health policies to continue covering dependent children through the end of the calendar year in which they turn 30, not merely age 26. That means a Florida 26-year-old whose parent has a fully-insured employer plan or a Marketplace plan may have four more years of continued coverage with no change in network, providers, or cost-sharing, provided they meet all four qualifying conditions. Understanding which type of plan your parent holds is therefore the most urgent first step, ideally completed before your 26th birthday to avoid any coverage gap. The Florida age-30 extension applies broadly but not universally: self-insured employer plans governed by federal ERISA law are not legally required to comply with Florida's state insurance mandates, and at companies with more than 200 employees, roughly 60 to 65 percent of workers hold self-insured plans. Checking that single fact with a parent's HR department can save thousands of dollars in unnecessary COBRA premiums or Marketplace transition costs.
introParagraphs.es: Cumplir 26 es la edad federal en que la cobertura de dependiente en el plan de salud de un padre debe terminar bajo la Ley de Cuidado de Salud Asequible. Para la mayoria de los estadounidenses, ese cumpleanos crea un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial (SEP) de 60 dias y obliga a buscar seguro de salud individual. Los residentes de Florida enfrentan el mismo reloj SEP, pero con una superposicion importante de ley estatal: el Estatuto de Seguros de Florida F.S. 627.6562 requiere que las aseguradoras de polizas de salud totalmente aseguradas y reguladas por el estado continuen cubriendo a los hijos dependientes hasta el fin del ano calendario en que cumplen 30 anos, no solo hasta los 26. Eso significa que un residente de Florida que cumple 26 anos y cuyo padre tiene un plan de empleador totalmente asegurado o un plan del Mercado puede tener cuatro anos mas de cobertura continua sin cambios en la red, los proveedores o el costo compartido, siempre que cumpla las cuatro condiciones de calificacion.

introParagraphs.en: Florida's Medicaid landscape adds another layer of complexity. Florida is one of the 10 non-expansion states that has not adopted ACA Medicaid expansion, which means the income-based Medicaid pathway available in 40 states plus DC does not exist for most 26-year-olds in Florida. Adults without dependent children must earn well below $4,300 per year to qualify for any Florida Medicaid category, creating a coverage gap for those earning between zero and 100 percent of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL), which is $15,960 for a single person in 2026. Florida residents in that gap are not eligible for either Medicaid or ACA premium tax credits. For those above 100 percent FPL, the ACA Marketplace at healthcare.gov is the primary option, with premium tax credits available up to 400 percent FPL ($63,840 single in 2026). The 400 percent FPL subsidy cliff returned for 2026 after the enhanced premium tax credits from the American Rescue Plan Act and Inflation Reduction Act expired on January 1, 2026. Florida's 2026 Marketplace has 16 carriers, including Florida Blue (covering all 67 counties) and Ambetter from Sunshine Health. For most Florida 26-year-olds, the decision path is: check the Florida extension first, then check employer coverage, then compare ACA Marketplace plans at healthcare.gov, then evaluate COBRA as a last resort. Check the ACA income limits to understand how your projected 2026 income affects subsidy size, and review Medicaid income limits to determine if any specific Florida Medicaid category applies to your situation.
introParagraphs.es: El panorama de Medicaid de Florida agrega otra capa de complejidad. Florida es uno de los 10 estados que no ha adoptado la expansion de Medicaid de la ACA, lo que significa que la ruta de Medicaid basada en ingresos disponible en 40 estados mas DC no existe para la mayoria de los jovenes de 26 anos en Florida. Los adultos sin hijos dependientes deben ganar muy por debajo de $4,300 al ano para calificar para cualquier categoria de Medicaid de Florida, creando una brecha de cobertura para quienes ganan entre cero y el 100 por ciento del Nivel Federal de Pobreza (FPL), que es $15,960 para una persona soltera en 2026. Para quienes estan por encima del 100 por ciento FPL, el Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov es la opcion principal, con creditos fiscales de prima disponibles hasta el 400 por ciento FPL ($63,840 individual en 2026).

name.en: Determine whether your parent's plan is fully-insured or self-insured
name.es: Determine si el plan de sus padres esta totalmente asegurado o autoasegurado

text.en: Call the HR department at your parent's employer and ask: Is this plan fully-insured or self-funded? If the plan is fully-insured (the insurance company bears the risk), Florida F.S. 627.6562 requires the insurer to offer continued coverage through the end of the calendar year you turn 30. If the plan is self-insured (the employer bears the risk under ERISA), the Florida extension does not legally apply. Check your parent's insurance card or the Summary Plan Description for the words 'self-funded' or 'self-insured.' Complete this check at least 30 days before your 26th birthday.
text.es: Llame al departamento de Recursos Humanos del empleador de sus padres y pregunte: Es este plan totalmente asegurado o autoasegurado? Si el plan es totalmente asegurado, la ley de Florida F.S. 627.6562 requiere que la aseguradora ofrezca cobertura continua hasta el fin del ano calendario en que cumpla 30. Si el plan es autoasegurado bajo ERISA, la extension de Florida no aplica legalmente. Revise la tarjeta de seguro de sus padres o la Descripcion del Plan para las palabras autoasegurado.

name.en: Confirm all four Florida extension conditions if the plan is fully-insured
name.es: Confirme las cuatro condiciones de la extension de Florida si el plan esta totalmente asegurado

text.en: To qualify under F.S. 627.6562, you must simultaneously meet: (1) you are unmarried; (2) you have no dependents of your own; (3) you are a Florida resident or a full-time or part-time student at any school; and (4) you are not covered under any other group health plan or individual policy and not entitled to Medicare. All four must be true on the date you seek coverage. If you gain employer coverage, marry, or gain a dependent, you lose extension eligibility going forward. If you previously held the parent's plan, dropped off after age 25, and then had a coverage gap exceeding 63 days under other insurance, re-enrollment under the Florida extension may be barred.
text.es: Para calificar bajo F.S. 627.6562, debe cumplir simultaneamente: (1) no esta casado; (2) no tiene dependientes propios; (3) es residente de Florida o estudiante a tiempo completo o parcial en cualquier escuela; y (4) no esta cubierto bajo ningun otro plan de salud grupal o poliza individual y no tiene derecho a Medicare. Las cuatro deben ser ciertas en la fecha en que solicita cobertura.

name.en: Calculate your projected 2026 income to check ACA subsidy eligibility
name.es: Calcule su ingreso proyectado 2026 para verificar elegibilidad de subsidios ACA

text.en: ACA Marketplace subsidies at healthcare.gov are based on your own projected Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) for 2026, not your parents' household income. A 26-year-old earning $30,000 may pay $80 to $200 per month for a Silver plan after premium tax credits, even if their parents earn $200,000. Estimate what you will earn from all sources for the rest of 2026: wages, freelance income, unemployment benefits if applicable, and investment income. Incomes from 100 percent FPL ($15,960 single) through 400 percent FPL ($63,840 single) qualify for premium tax credits. Incomes below 100 percent FPL fall into Florida's Medicaid coverage gap for most single adults.
text.es: Los subsidios del Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov se basan en su propio Ingreso Bruto Ajustado Modificado (MAGI) proyectado para 2026, no en el ingreso del hogar de sus padres. Un joven de 26 anos que gana $30,000 puede pagar $80 a $200 al mes por un plan Silver despues de los creditos fiscales de prima. Estime lo que ganara de todas las fuentes para el resto de 2026: salarios, ingreso independiente, beneficios por desempleo si aplica, e ingreso de inversiones.

name.en: Apply at healthcare.gov during your 60-day Marketplace SEP
name.es: Solicite en healthcare.gov durante su SEP del Mercado de 60 dias

text.en: Log in to healthcare.gov or call 1-800-318-2596 and select 'Turning 26 or losing dependent coverage' as your qualifying life event. Enter your coverage termination date. Compare Florida Blue, Ambetter from Sunshine Health, and other 2026 Florida Marketplace plans by ZIP code. Catastrophic plans are available if you are under 30 and have an income below 250 percent FPL or qualify for a hardship exemption. Silver plans with cost-sharing reductions offer the best value for incomes under 250 percent FPL ($39,900 single). Enroll by Day 60 from your coverage loss date to avoid a gap.
text.es: Inicie sesion en healthcare.gov o llame al 1-800-318-2596 y seleccione Cumplir 26 o perder cobertura de dependiente como su evento calificador. Ingrese la fecha de terminacion de cobertura. Compare los planes del Mercado 2026 de Florida, incluyendo Florida Blue y Ambetter de Sunshine Health, por codigo postal.

name.en: Evaluate COBRA as a last-resort bridge if you have ongoing specialist treatment
name.es: Evalue COBRA como puente de ultimo recurso si tiene tratamiento especializado continuo

text.en: COBRA continuation on your parent's Florida plan costs 102 percent of the full premium, typically $400 to $900 per month for an individual in 2026, and lasts up to 36 months for aging-off a parent's plan. Elect COBRA only if you have ongoing treatment with a specific Florida specialist not in any Marketplace network, or if the parent's plan deductible is nearly met and you have a procedure scheduled before December 31. Submit your COBRA election to the plan administrator within 60 days of receiving the qualifying event notice. Compare COBRA cost against Marketplace Silver plan premiums using healthcare.gov's plan comparison tool before deciding.
text.es: La continuacion COBRA del plan de Florida de sus padres cuesta el 102 por ciento de la prima completa, tipicamente $400 a $900 al mes para un individuo en 2026, y dura hasta 36 meses para salir del plan de los padres. Elija COBRA solo si tiene tratamiento continuo con un especialista de Florida especifico que no esta en ninguna red del Mercado.

name.en: Submit your qualifying event documentation and enroll before Day 60
name.es: Envie la documentacion del evento calificador e inscribase antes del Dia 60

text.en: healthcare.gov may verify your qualifying life event automatically, but be ready to submit a coverage termination letter from your parent's insurer or employer confirming your name and coverage end date. Keep this document (often called an HIPAA certificate of creditable coverage or a coverage termination notice) for your records and for your 2026 federal tax return reconciliation using Form 1095-A. Enroll in your chosen plan before the 60-day window closes. Your new coverage typically starts the first day of the month after you enroll, or the first day of the month after your coverage loss if you enroll before losing coverage.
text.es: healthcare.gov puede verificar su evento calificador automaticamente, pero este listo para enviar una carta de terminacion de cobertura del asegurador o empleador de sus padres confirmando su nombre y fecha de fin de cobertura. Guarde este documento (a menudo llamado certificado HIPAA de cobertura acreditable) para sus registros y para la reconciliacion de su declaracion de impuestos federal 2026 usando el Formulario 1095-A.

footnote.en: Florida has not expanded Medicaid under the ACA, so most single adults without dependents do not qualify for Florida Medicaid based on income alone. The 2026 ACA subsidy cliff returned after enhanced premium tax credits expired January 1, 2026: incomes above 400% FPL ($63,840 single) receive no premium tax credit. The Florida age-30 extension applies only to state-regulated fully-insured plans, not self-insured ERISA plans. Cost figures are estimates for 2026.
footnote.es: Florida no ha expandido Medicaid bajo la ACA, por lo que la mayoria de adultos solteros sin dependientes no califican para Medicaid de Florida basandose solo en el ingreso. El precipicio de subsidio ACA 2026 regreso despues de que los creditos fiscales de prima mejorados expiraron el 1 de enero de 2026: los ingresos por encima del 400% FPL ($63,840 individual) no reciben credito fiscal de prima. La extension de Florida hasta los 30 aplica solo a planes totalmente asegurados regulados por el estado.

intro.en: The most costly mistakes Florida 26-year-olds make when transitioning off a parent's health plan:
intro.es: Los errores mas costosos que cometen los jovenes de 26 anos en Florida al salir del plan de salud de sus padres:

items.en: Assuming the Florida age-30 extension applies to all employer plans. Florida F.S. 627.6562 covers only state-regulated, fully-insured plans. Self-insured plans at large employers, which cover an estimated 60 to 65 percent of workers at companies with 200 or more employees, are governed by ERISA and not required to offer the Florida extension. Call HR before your 26th birthday to confirm plan type in writing.
items.es: Asumir que la extension de Florida hasta los 30 aplica a todos los planes del empleador. F.S. 627.6562 cubre solo planes totalmente asegurados regulados por el estado. Los planes autoasegurados en grandes empleadores, que cubren aproximadamente el 60 a 65 por ciento de los trabajadores en empresas con 200 o mas empleados, estan regidos por ERISA y no estan obligados a ofrecer la extension de Florida. Llame a RR.HH. antes de su cumpleanos 26 para confirmar el tipo de plan por escrito.

items.en: Missing the 60-day SEP window while waiting to decide. The Marketplace SEP starts the date coverage ends, not when you begin shopping. Starting your search on Day 50 reduces comparison time and may delay your new plan's coverage start date, leaving a gap.
items.es: Perder la ventana SEP de 60 dias mientras espera decidir. El SEP del Mercado comienza el dia que termina la cobertura, no cuando empieza a buscar. Comenzar su busqueda en el Dia 50 reduce el tiempo de comparacion y puede retrasar la fecha de inicio de cobertura de su nuevo plan.

items.en: Using parental household income to estimate ACA subsidy eligibility. ACA subsidies at age 26 are calculated based on your own projected 2026 MAGI and your own household, not your parents' income. A 26-year-old earning $28,000 likely qualifies for a substantial premium tax credit regardless of parental income.
items.es: Usar el ingreso del hogar de los padres para estimar la elegibilidad de subsidios ACA. Los subsidios ACA a los 26 anos se calculan basados en su propio MAGI proyectado 2026 y su propio hogar, no en el ingreso de sus padres. Un joven de 26 anos que gana $28,000 probablemente califica para un credito fiscal de prima sustancial independientemente del ingreso de los padres.

items.en: Defaulting to COBRA without comparing Florida Blue or Ambetter Marketplace premiums. COBRA charges 102 percent of the full premium, typically $400 to $900 per month for an individual. Most 26-year-olds earning under $63,840 (400% FPL single, 2026) find ACA Marketplace Silver plans substantially cheaper after premium tax credits. Compare at healthcare.gov before electing COBRA.
items.es: Optar por COBRA sin comparar las primas del Mercado de Florida Blue o Ambetter. COBRA cobra el 102 por ciento de la prima completa, tipicamente $400 a $900 al mes para un individuo. La mayoria de los jovenes de 26 anos que ganan menos de $63,840 (400% FPL individual, 2026) encuentran los planes Silver del Mercado ACA sustancialmente mas baratos despues de los creditos fiscales de prima.

items.en: Not checking employer coverage before age 26. If your job offers health benefits, you typically have a 30-day special enrollment window from your 26th birthday or the date your parent's plan drops you, whichever is later. Missing that employer window closes off another coverage path.
items.es: No verificar la cobertura del empleador antes de los 26 anos. Si su trabajo ofrece beneficios de salud, generalmente tiene una ventana de inscripcion especial de 30 dias desde su cumpleanos 26 o la fecha en que el plan de sus padres lo da de baja. Perder esa ventana del empleador cierra otra ruta de cobertura.

items.en: Forgetting to file Form 1095-A at tax time. If you enroll in an ACA Marketplace plan through healthcare.gov, you will receive a Form 1095-A in January 2027. This form is required to reconcile your premium tax credit on your 2026 federal tax return. Missing it can delay your refund or create an unexpected balance due.
items.es: Olvidar presentar el Formulario 1095-A en la declaracion de impuestos. Si se inscribe en un plan del Mercado ACA a traves de healthcare.gov, recibira un Formulario 1095-A en enero de 2027. Este formulario es necesario para reconciliar su credito fiscal de prima en su declaracion de impuestos federal 2026.

heading.en: Florida F.S. 627.6562: The Age-30 Dependent Coverage Extension in Detail
heading.es: Florida F.S. 627.6562: La Extension de Cobertura de Dependiente hasta los 30 en Detalle

paragraphs.en: Florida Insurance Statute F.S. 627.6562 requires insurers of state-regulated health policies to cover dependent children through the end of the calendar year in which they turn 30, extending the federal ACA floor of age 26 by four additional years. The law applies to individual health plans sold through the Florida Marketplace, small-group fully-insured employer plans (typically employers with fewer than 50 full-time employees who purchase coverage from an insurer), and large-group fully-insured employer plans (employers that buy traditional group insurance rather than self-funding). The phrase 'end of the calendar year' matters: if you turn 30 on February 10, 2030, your coverage can continue through December 31, 2030, not just through your birthday.
paragraphs.es: El Estatuto de Seguros de Florida F.S. 627.6562 requiere que las aseguradoras de polizas de salud reguladas por el estado cubran a los hijos dependientes hasta el fin del ano calendario en que cumplen 30 anos, extendiendo el minimo federal de la ACA de los 26 anos por cuatro anos adicionales. La ley aplica a planes de salud individuales vendidos a traves del Mercado de Florida, planes de empleadores pequenos totalmente asegurados, y planes de empleadores grandes totalmente asegurados.

paragraphs.en: ERISA preemption is the most important limitation. Employers who self-insure their health benefit plans are governed by the federal Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA), which preempts state insurance mandates. Florida law cannot legally require self-insured employers to offer the age-30 extension. At large companies (200 or more employees), approximately 60 to 65 percent of workers are covered by self-insured plans. Some large Florida employers voluntarily mirror the state extension as an HR benefit, but that is their choice, not a legal requirement. The only reliable way to know: ask the parent's HR department to confirm in writing whether the plan is fully-insured or self-funded, and request a copy of the Summary Plan Description (SPD) page that describes plan type.
paragraphs.es: La prevencion de ERISA es la limitacion mas importante. Los empleadores que autoaseguran sus planes de beneficios de salud estan regidos por la Ley Federal de Seguridad de Ingresos de Jubilacion de Empleados (ERISA), que preempts los mandatos estatales de seguros. La ley de Florida no puede legalmente requerir que los empleadores autoasegurados ofrezcan la extension hasta los 30 anos.

paragraphs.en: Four conditions must all be met simultaneously and continuously to qualify for the Florida extension. First, you must be unmarried. Second, you must have no dependents of your own (no child, no dependent). Third, you must be either a resident of Florida or a full-time or part-time student at any educational institution. Fourth, you must not be covered under any other group health plan or individual plan and must not be entitled to Medicare benefits. All four conditions are ongoing: if you marry, gain a dependent, move out of Florida without being enrolled in school, gain access to an employer plan, or become Medicare-entitled, your eligibility ends going forward. The 63-day rule also applies: if you previously held the parent's plan, left it after age 25, and then had a coverage gap in other insurance exceeding 63 consecutive days, the statute bars re-enrollment under the Florida extension.
paragraphs.es: Cuatro condiciones deben cumplirse simultaneamente y continuamente para calificar para la extension de Florida. Primero, debe estar soltero. Segundo, no debe tener dependientes propios. Tercero, debe ser residente de Florida o estudiante a tiempo completo o parcial en cualquier institucion educativa. Cuarto, no debe estar cubierto bajo ningun otro plan de salud grupal o individual y no debe tener derecho a Medicare.

heading.en: Florida Marketplace Options in 2026: Florida Blue, Ambetter, and Your Decision Criteria
heading.es: Opciones del Mercado de Florida en 2026: Florida Blue, Ambetter y Sus Criterios de Decision

paragraphs.en: Florida's 2026 ACA Marketplace has 16 carriers offering plans in at least one county, with Florida Blue (Blue Cross Blue Shield of Florida) covering all 67 Florida counties and Ambetter from Sunshine Health covering 63 counties. Both offer Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Catastrophic plan tiers. For 26-year-olds, Catastrophic plans are available through age 29: they carry the lowest premium but the highest deductible, equal to the 2026 ACA out-of-pocket maximum of $10,600 for an individual, with three primary care visits covered before the deductible kicks in. Catastrophic plans make sense only for healthy young adults who primarily want protection against major medical events and whose income qualifies for a hardship exemption or is below 250 percent FPL. Silver plans with cost-sharing reductions are generally the best value for 26-year-olds earning between 100 and 250 percent FPL ($15,960 to $39,900 single in 2026), since Silver CSR plans significantly reduce deductibles and out-of-pocket costs beyond the premium savings.
paragraphs.es: El Mercado ACA 2026 de Florida tiene 16 aseguradoras que ofrecen planes en al menos un condado, con Florida Blue (Blue Cross Blue Shield de Florida) cubriendo los 67 condados de Florida y Ambetter de Sunshine Health cubriendo 63 condados. Ambas ofrecen niveles de plan Bronze, Silver, Gold y Catastrofico. Para jovenes de 26 anos, los planes Catastroficos estan disponibles hasta los 29 anos.

paragraphs.en: Premium tax credits in 2026 are calculated on a sliding scale from 100 percent to 400 percent FPL. The 2026 subsidy cliff is back: a 26-year-old earning $64,000 per year (just above 400 percent FPL) receives no premium tax credit at all, while a 26-year-old earning $63,800 (just below 400 percent FPL) may receive a credit of several hundred dollars per month. For 26-year-olds in Florida earning between 150 and 300 percent FPL ($23,940 to $47,880 single), a Silver plan from Florida Blue or Ambetter typically costs between $40 and $180 per month after premium tax credits in most Florida counties. Compare plans based on your specific Florida county and ZIP code at healthcare.gov, since network composition and premiums differ significantly between Miami-Dade, Broward, Palm Beach, Orange, Hillsborough, Duval, and rural Florida counties. Use the ACA income limits page to verify your 2026 subsidy eligibility before enrolling.
paragraphs.es: Los creditos fiscales de prima en 2026 se calculan en una escala deslizante del 100 por ciento al 400 por ciento FPL. El precipicio de subsidio 2026 ha regresado: un joven de 26 anos que gana $64,000 al ano (justo por encima del 400 por ciento FPL) no recibe ningun credito fiscal de prima, mientras que uno que gana $63,800 (justo por debajo del 400 por ciento FPL) puede recibir un credito de varios cientos de dolares al mes.

heading.en: COBRA vs Florida Age-30 Extension vs ACA Marketplace: The 2026 Decision Guide for Florida 26-Year-Olds
heading.es: COBRA vs Extension de Florida hasta 30 vs Mercado ACA: Guia de Decision 2026 para Jovenes de 26 Anos en Florida

paragraphs.en: Three main pathways open for Florida 26-year-olds at the coverage transition point. The Florida age-30 extension is the most cost-effective when available: staying on a fully-insured parent plan means the same network, same ongoing deductible accumulation, and the same cost-share as before, with no coverage gap or enrollment delay. For a 26-year-old mid-year who has already satisfied $2,000 of a $3,000 deductible on the parent's plan, the extension preserves that credit and prevents the deductible from resetting under a new plan. The ACA Marketplace SEP at healthcare.gov is the primary alternative when the Florida extension does not apply. Most 26-year-olds qualify for their own income-based subsidies, which are often more favorable than parental household income would suggest: a 26-year-old earning $32,000 in 2026 (200 percent FPL) typically qualifies for a Silver plan at Florida Blue or Ambetter for $100 to $200 per month, with cost-sharing reductions that lower the effective deductible to $1,000 to $2,000 rather than the full Silver deductible. COBRA should be considered a last resort for most Florida 26-year-olds: at 102 percent of the full premium, it costs $400 to $900 per month for an individual, and rarely makes financial sense when subsidized Marketplace coverage is available. The two scenarios where COBRA offers real value are (1) ongoing treatment with a specialist who is not in any Florida Marketplace plan's network, making continuity of care worth the higher cost, and (2) a parent's plan deductible that is nearly or fully met for the calendar year, with a significant planned procedure or surgery before December 31 that would cost more out-of-pocket if the deductible reset under a new Marketplace plan.
paragraphs.es: Tres rutas principales se abren para los jovenes de 26 anos en Florida en el punto de transicion de cobertura. La extension de Florida hasta los 30 es la mas rentable cuando esta disponible: permanecer en el plan totalmente asegurado de los padres significa la misma red, la misma acumulacion de deducible en curso, y el mismo costo compartido que antes. El SEP del Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov es la alternativa principal cuando la extension de Florida no aplica. La mayoria de los jovenes de 26 anos califican para subsidios basados en su propio ingreso, que a menudo son mas favorables de lo que sugeriria el ingreso del hogar de los padres. COBRA debe considerarse un ultimo recurso para la mayoria de los jovenes de 26 anos en Florida: al 102 por ciento de la prima completa, cuesta $400 a $900 al mes para un individuo.

heading.en: Florida Medicaid and the Coverage Gap for 26-Year-Olds in 2026
heading.es: Medicaid de Florida y la Brecha de Cobertura para Jovenes de 26 Anos en 2026

paragraphs.en: Florida Medicaid covers pregnant women (up to 191 percent FPL), children and teens under Florida KidCare (the state CHIP program, at incomes up to approximately 200 percent FPL for Medicaid and higher for Florida KidCare MediKids), and certain disabled or caretaker adults, but it does not cover most single, childless adults regardless of income. Florida is one of the 10 non-expansion states as of 2026, along with Alabama, Georgia, Kansas, Mississippi, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Wisconsin, and Wyoming. An estimated 388,000 Florida residents fall into the coverage gap, earning between zero and 100 percent FPL and therefore ineligible for both Florida Medicaid and ACA premium tax credits. For a 26-year-old, 100 percent FPL is $15,960 annually in 2026. Adults above 100 percent FPL can access ACA Marketplace subsidies. Adults below 100 percent FPL and not in a specific Medicaid category face uninsured status or a Catastrophic plan (if they qualify for a hardship exemption). Apply for Florida Medicaid through the ACCESS Florida system at myflorida.com/accessflorida or by calling the Florida DCF at 1-866-762-2237. Florida KidCare enrollment for dependent children can be initiated at floridakidcare.org.
paragraphs.es: Medicaid de Florida cubre a mujeres embarazadas (hasta el 191 por ciento FPL), ninos y adolescentes bajo Florida KidCare (el programa CHIP del estado), y ciertos adultos discapacitados o cuidadores, pero no cubre a la mayoria de adultos solteros sin hijos independientemente del ingreso. Florida es uno de los 10 estados sin expansion en 2026. Un estimado de 388,000 residentes de Florida caen en la brecha de cobertura, ganando entre cero y el 100 por ciento FPL y por lo tanto no elegibles ni para Medicaid de Florida ni para creditos fiscales de prima ACA. Solicite Medicaid de Florida a traves del sistema ACCESS Florida en myflorida.com/accessflorida.

heading.en: COBRA vs Florida Age-30 Extension vs ACA Marketplace: Which Should You Choose in 2026?
heading.es: COBRA vs Extension de Florida hasta 30 vs Mercado ACA: Cual Debe Elegir en 2026?

body.en: Florida 26-year-olds face a three-way coverage decision that most Americans in other states do not have. Florida F.S. 627.6562 makes the age-30 extension the dominant first choice when available: staying on a fully-insured parent plan costs the same as before, preserves the deductible already met for the year, keeps existing providers, and avoids any enrollment delay. For a Florida 26-year-old mid-year on a parent plan with $1,500 already credited toward a $3,000 deductible, the extension saves that $1,500 and avoids restarting a new plan's deductible, a material benefit worth hundreds of dollars in out-of-pocket savings. ACA Marketplace plans at healthcare.gov are the right choice when the Florida extension does not apply (self-insured ERISA plans) and when individual income falls between 100 and 400 percent FPL ($15,960 to $63,840 single in 2026). Florida Blue and Ambetter both cover all major Florida counties, and most 26-year-olds pay $40 to $200 per month for a Silver plan after premium tax credits at incomes between 150 and 300 percent FPL. COBRA is rarely the right answer for Florida 26-year-olds who qualify for Marketplace subsidies: at 102 percent of the full premium, $400 to $900 per month for individual coverage is typically three to five times the cost of a subsidized Silver plan. The one exception worth noting is continuity of care: if a 26-year-old has an ongoing treatment relationship with a specific specialist at Cleveland Clinic Florida, Moffitt Cancer Center, or another Florida tertiary-care provider who is not in any Marketplace network, COBRA may provide temporary continuity while a transition plan is arranged.
body.es: Los jovenes de 26 anos en Florida enfrentan una decision de cobertura de tres vias que la mayoria de los estadounidenses en otros estados no tienen. Florida F.S. 627.6562 hace que la extension hasta los 30 sea la primera opcion dominante cuando esta disponible: permanecer en el plan totalmente asegurado de los padres cuesta lo mismo que antes, preserva el deducible ya cumplido para el ano, mantiene los proveedores existentes y evita cualquier retraso en la inscripcion. Los planes del Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov son la opcion correcta cuando la extension de Florida no aplica y cuando el ingreso individual cae entre el 100 y el 400 por ciento FPL ($15,960 a $63,840 individual en 2026). COBRA rara vez es la respuesta correcta para los jovenes de 26 anos en Florida que califican para subsidios del Mercado.

en.question: How long do I have to enroll in new coverage after turning 26 in Florida?
en.answer: You have 60 days from the date your parent's plan coverage ends to enroll in a new plan through the ACA Marketplace Special Enrollment Period (SEP) at healthcare.gov. You can also begin shopping up to 60 days before your coverage ends. Most Florida parent plans end coverage on the last day of the birthday month, so if you turn 26 on July 15, 2026, coverage typically ends July 31, 2026, and your SEP window runs from July 31 through September 28, 2026. If you qualify for the Florida F.S. 627.6562 age-30 extension on a fully-insured parent plan, no Marketplace SEP deadline applies since you remain on the existing plan. COBRA must be elected within 60 days of receiving the qualifying event notice from the plan administrator.

en.question: What is the Florida age-30 health insurance extension and who qualifies?
en.answer: Florida Statute F.S. 627.6562 requires insurers of state-regulated, fully-insured health plans to offer continued coverage for dependent children through the end of the calendar year in which they turn 30, extending the federal ACA dependent coverage floor of age 26 by four years. To qualify, you must simultaneously meet all four conditions: (1) you are unmarried; (2) you have no dependents of your own; (3) you are a Florida resident or a full-time or part-time student at any educational institution; and (4) you are not covered under any other group or individual health plan and are not entitled to Medicare. The plan must also be fully-insured. Self-insured employer plans governed by ERISA are not required to comply with Florida insurance law mandates.

en.question: Does the Florida age-30 extension apply if my parent's employer is a large company?
en.answer: Not necessarily. Florida's age-30 extension under F.S. 627.6562 applies only to state-regulated, fully-insured plans. Most large employers (200 or more employees) use self-insured plans governed by federal ERISA law, which preempts Florida state insurance mandates. At these employers, the Florida extension does not apply as a legal requirement, though some voluntarily offer it. The only way to know for certain: ask the parent's HR department to confirm in writing whether the plan is 'fully-insured' (the insurer bears risk) or 'self-funded' (the employer bears risk). Review the Summary Plan Description (SPD) for the plan type designation.

en.question: What is my SEP window for the ACA Marketplace after turning 26 in Florida?
en.answer: Your 60-day Special Enrollment Period (SEP) for the ACA Marketplace at healthcare.gov opens the day your parent-plan coverage ends and closes 60 days later. For example, if coverage ends on September 30, 2026, your SEP runs from September 30 through November 28, 2026. Coverage under your new Marketplace plan typically starts the first day of the month after you enroll. If you enroll before your coverage loss date, your new plan can start the day after your current coverage ends. You select 'Turning 26 or losing dependent coverage' as your qualifying life event when applying at healthcare.gov.

en.question: Can I get Medicaid in Florida when I turn 26?
en.answer: Most single, childless 26-year-olds in Florida cannot qualify for Florida Medicaid because Florida has not expanded Medicaid under the ACA. The income limit for non-disabled, non-pregnant adults without dependent children is approximately $355 per month, which is well below the income level of most working 26-year-olds. Florida Medicaid does cover pregnant women up to 191 percent FPL, children and teens up to certain FPL thresholds through Florida KidCare (the state CHIP program), and certain disabled individuals. If your income falls below 100 percent FPL ($15,960 single in 2026) and you do not qualify for a specific Florida Medicaid category, you fall into the coverage gap. Apply through ACCESS Florida at myflorida.com/accessflorida or call Florida DCF at 1-866-762-2237 to check specific eligibility.

en.question: How do ACA subsidies work for a 26-year-old in Florida in 2026?
en.answer: ACA premium tax credits are based on your own projected 2026 Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI), not your parents' income. For a 26-year-old in Florida in 2026, premium tax credits are available for incomes from 100 percent FPL ($15,960 single) through 400 percent FPL ($63,840 single). The 2026 subsidy cliff returned after enhanced premium tax credits from ARPA and the IRA expired January 1, 2026: incomes above 400 percent FPL receive no credit. Most 26-year-olds earning $25,000 to $45,000 in 2026 qualify for Silver plans at Florida Blue or Ambetter for $40 to $180 per month in most Florida counties after premium tax credits. Use the ACA income limits reference to calculate your expected credit size before comparing plans at healthcare.gov.

en.question: What is COBRA and should I elect it at age 26 in Florida?
en.answer: COBRA is a federal law that lets you continue your parent's group health plan after losing dependent coverage, at 102 percent of the full premium (employer plus employee share plus 2 percent administration fee). For an individual in Florida in 2026, typical COBRA premiums run $400 to $900 per month. COBRA lasts up to 36 months for aging off a parent's plan (this is longer than the 18-month duration for job loss). For most Florida 26-year-olds earning between $15,960 and $63,840 (100 to 400 percent FPL), ACA Marketplace plans are substantially cheaper after premium tax credits. Elect COBRA only if you have ongoing treatment with a specific specialist who is not in any Florida Marketplace network, or if the parent's plan deductible is almost fully met and you have a major procedure planned before year-end. Submit your COBRA election within 60 days of receiving the qualifying event notice.

en.question: What documents do I need to apply for a Florida Marketplace plan after turning 26?
en.answer: To enroll at healthcare.gov using the turning-26 SEP, gather these documents: (1) a coverage termination letter from your parent's insurer or employer HR department confirming your name, coverage end date, and reason for termination; (2) your Social Security number; (3) your Florida home address or ZIP code for plan lookup; (4) projected 2026 income from all sources (wages, freelance, any unemployment benefits); and (5) bank account or credit card for your first premium payment. If you receive premium tax credits, you will get a Form 1095-A from healthcare.gov in January 2027, which you must include on your 2026 federal tax return to reconcile your credit. Keep the coverage termination letter for tax records and to satisfy any Section 9831 (HIPAA) creditable coverage documentation if you transition between plans.

es.question: Cuanto tiempo tengo para inscribirme en nueva cobertura despues de cumplir 26 en Florida?
es.answer: Tiene 60 dias desde que termina la cobertura del plan de sus padres para inscribirse en un nuevo plan a traves del Periodo de Inscripcion Especial (SEP) del Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov. Tambien puede comenzar a comparar hasta 60 dias antes de que termine su cobertura. La mayoria de los planes de padres en Florida terminan la cobertura el ultimo dia del mes de cumpleanos, por lo que si cumple 26 el 15 de julio de 2026, la cobertura tipicamente termina el 31 de julio de 2026, y su ventana SEP va del 31 de julio al 28 de septiembre de 2026. Si califica para la extension de Florida hasta los 30 anos bajo F.S. 627.6562 en un plan totalmente asegurado, no aplica ningun plazo de SEP del Mercado.

es.question: Que es la extension de seguro de salud de Florida hasta los 30 y quien califica?
es.answer: El Estatuto de Florida F.S. 627.6562 requiere que las aseguradoras de planes de salud totalmente asegurados regulados por el estado ofrezcan cobertura continua para hijos dependientes hasta el fin del ano calendario en que cumplen 30 anos, extendiendo el minimo federal ACA de los 26 anos por cuatro anos. Para calificar, debe cumplir simultaneamente las cuatro condiciones: (1) no esta casado; (2) no tiene dependientes propios; (3) es residente de Florida o estudiante a tiempo completo o parcial en cualquier institucion educativa; y (4) no esta cubierto bajo ningun otro plan de salud grupal o individual y no tiene derecho a Medicare. El plan tambien debe estar totalmente asegurado.

es.question: Aplica la extension de Florida hasta los 30 si el empleador de mis padres es una empresa grande?
es.answer: No necesariamente. La extension de Florida hasta los 30 bajo F.S. 627.6562 aplica solo a planes totalmente asegurados regulados por el estado. La mayoria de los grandes empleadores (200 o mas empleados) usan planes autoasegurados regidos por la ley federal ERISA, que preempts los mandatos estatales de seguros de Florida. En estos empleadores, la extension de Florida no aplica como requisito legal, aunque algunos la ofrecen voluntariamente. La unica forma de saberlo con certeza: pida al departamento de RR.HH. de sus padres que confirme por escrito si el plan es totalmente asegurado (la aseguradora asume el riesgo) o autoasegurado (el empleador asume el riesgo).

es.question: Cual es mi ventana SEP para el Mercado ACA despues de cumplir 26 en Florida?
es.answer: Su Periodo de Inscripcion Especial (SEP) de 60 dias para el Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov comienza el dia que termina la cobertura del plan de sus padres y cierra 60 dias despues. Por ejemplo, si la cobertura termina el 30 de septiembre de 2026, su SEP va del 30 de septiembre al 28 de noviembre de 2026. La cobertura bajo su nuevo plan del Mercado tipicamente comienza el primer dia del mes despues de que se inscribe. Seleccione Cumplir 26 o perder cobertura de dependiente como su evento calificador al solicitar en healthcare.gov.

es.question: Puedo obtener Medicaid en Florida cuando cumpla 26?
es.answer: La mayoria de los adultos solteros de 26 anos sin hijos en Florida no pueden calificar para Medicaid de Florida porque Florida no ha expandido Medicaid bajo la ACA. El limite de ingreso para adultos no discapacitados sin hijos dependientes es aproximadamente $355 al mes, muy por debajo del nivel de ingreso de la mayoria de los jovenes de 26 anos que trabajan. Medicaid de Florida cubre a mujeres embarazadas hasta el 191 por ciento FPL, ninos y adolescentes a traves de Florida KidCare (el programa CHIP del estado), y ciertos individuos discapacitados. Si su ingreso cae por debajo del 100 por ciento FPL ($15,960 individual en 2026) y no califica para una categoria especifica de Medicaid de Florida, cae en la brecha de cobertura. Solicite a traves de ACCESS Florida en myflorida.com/accessflorida.

es.question: Como funcionan los subsidios ACA para un joven de 26 anos en Florida en 2026?
es.answer: Los creditos fiscales de prima ACA se basan en su propio Ingreso Bruto Ajustado Modificado (MAGI) proyectado 2026, no en el ingreso de sus padres. Para un joven de 26 anos en Florida en 2026, los creditos fiscales de prima estan disponibles para ingresos del 100 por ciento FPL ($15,960 individual) hasta el 400 por ciento FPL ($63,840 individual). El precipicio de subsidio 2026 regreso despues de que los creditos fiscales de prima mejorados de ARPA y la IRA expiraron el 1 de enero de 2026: los ingresos por encima del 400 por ciento FPL no reciben credito. La mayoria de los jovenes de 26 anos que ganan entre $25,000 y $45,000 en 2026 califican para planes Silver de Florida Blue o Ambetter por $40 a $180 al mes en la mayoria de los condados de Florida despues de los creditos fiscales de prima.

es.question: Que es COBRA y debo elegirlo a los 26 anos en Florida?
es.answer: COBRA es una ley federal que le permite continuar el plan de salud grupal de sus padres despues de perder la cobertura de dependiente, al 102 por ciento de la prima completa. Para un individuo en Florida en 2026, las primas tipicas de COBRA van de $400 a $900 al mes. COBRA dura hasta 36 meses para salir del plan de los padres. Para la mayoria de los jovenes de 26 anos en Florida que ganan entre $15,960 y $63,840 (100 a 400 por ciento FPL), los planes del Mercado ACA son sustancialmente mas baratos despues de los creditos fiscales de prima. Elija COBRA solo si tiene tratamiento continuo con un especialista especifico que no esta en ninguna red del Mercado de Florida.

es.question: Que documentos necesito para solicitar un plan del Mercado de Florida despues de cumplir 26?
es.answer: Para inscribirse en healthcare.gov usando el SEP de cumplir 26, reuna estos documentos: (1) una carta de terminacion de cobertura del asegurador o departamento de RR.HH. del empleador de sus padres confirmando su nombre, fecha de fin de cobertura y razon de terminacion; (2) su numero de Seguro Social; (3) su direccion de Florida o codigo postal para busqueda de planes; (4) ingreso proyectado 2026 de todas las fuentes; y (5) cuenta bancaria o tarjeta de credito para su primer pago de prima. Si recibe creditos fiscales de prima, recibira un Formulario 1095-A de healthcare.gov en enero de 2027, que debe incluir en su declaracion de impuestos federal 2026 para reconciliar su credito.
